components.name: Dark CTA Button
components.description: Compact decisive action button used for news card CTAs.
components.css: .ds-btn-dark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; padding: 6px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #27272a, rgba(0,0,0,0.9)); color: #ffffff; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; transition: opacity 150ms ease-out, transform 75ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-dark:hover { opacity: 0.9; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-dark:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #71717a; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-icon { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Neutral Status Chip
components.description: Small pill for section labels and status metadata.
components.css: .ds-chip-neutral { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid rgba(212, 212, 216, 0.7); border-radius: 9999px; background: #ffffff; padding: 4px 12px; color: #3f3f46; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Editorial Card
components.description: Quiet news/content card with strong title hierarchy and soft zinc surface.
components.html:
Татарский центр «Идел» в Алматы

Центр объединяет татар и башкир, развивает культурные инициативы и поддерживает живую связь поколений.
components.css: .ds-card-editorial { max-width: 520px; border: 1px solid rgba(161, 161, 170, 0.4); border-radius: 24px; background: #fafafa; padding: 24px; color: #18181b; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(212, 212, 216, 0.3); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-card-editorial h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: #18181b; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.15; letter-spacing: -0.025em; text-wrap: balance; } .ds-card-editorial p { margin: 0; color: #3f3f46; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.625; text-wrap: pretty; }

components.name: Instagram Action
components.description: Tinted social action pill for Instagram links.
components.css: .ds-action-instagram { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 12px; background: #fdf2f8; color: #be185d; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-action-instagram:hover { background: #fce7f3; } .ds-action-instagram:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ec4899; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.description: Compact black square that opens the mobile navigation overlay.

narrative.overview:
The system should feel like the living public board of a cultural center: current, practical, welcoming, and grounded in real people. It is a brand/community site, not an app shell and not a corporate campaign. White space, direct Russian copy, local photos, compact navigation, and simple action links carry the experience.

The visual language is local, human, cultural, and clear. It uses a white editorial base with zinc text, black practical calls to action, and small community color fields for sections and tags. It explicitly rejects a generic corporate landing page, stock-cultural festival templates, anonymous NGO polish, heavy folklore ornament, and replacing real center/event photos with generic imagery.
keyCharacteristics: White, readable editorial surfaces with strong zinc ink.
Compact cards and practical buttons rather than decorative marketing blocks.
Real community content first: news, activists, events, gallery, contacts.
Small color accents for meaning and section identity, never as generic decoration.
Rounded surfaces are present, but the site should not drift into pillowy SaaS styling.

rules.name: The Community Accent Rule
rules.body: Color marks a job: social, map, new status, event block, or section identity. Do not spread accent color just to make the page feel designed.

rules.name: The White Hall Rule
rules.body: The site starts from a white public-room surface. Warmth comes from content, photos, and accents, not from beige body backgrounds.

rules.name: The Plain Russian Rule
rules.body: Prioritize readable Russian text over decorative styling. Do not use ornate display fonts or artificial folk styling unless explicitly requested.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Headings should use balanced wrapping and avoid overflow on mobile; long Russian words must fit before any visual flourish is accepted.

rules.name: The Flat-First Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are readable at rest through color, border, and spacing. Shadow may support a state or card boundary, but it should not become the main visual idea.

dos: Do keep White Hall, Zinc Ink, and compact navigation as the baseline for public pages.
Do use real center/event/activist photos whenever the content calls for imagery.
Do use community color accents only when they communicate role: social, map, new status, section identity, or event grouping.
Do preserve readable Russian hierarchy with balanced headings, strong titles, and body lines around 65-75ch.
Do keep action paths practical: Instagram, 2GIS, contacts, events, and stories should be obvious.
donts: Don't make the site feel like a generic corporate landing page.
Don't use a stock cultural festival template, anonymous NGO brochure styling, or decorative folklore motifs as a substitute for real content.
Don't replace real center and event photos with generic imagery.
Don't overuse ornamental ethnic motifs or redesign away from the existing editorial/community character without an explicit request.
Don't repeat tiny uppercase tracked labels above every section as generic scaffolding.
Don't pair decorative 1px borders with large soft shadows on every card; choose structural border or light elevation deliberately.
